title: Consumer safety moves through injury surveillance, recalls, import screening, and platform removal
source_unit: US Consumer Product Safety Commission FY2024 Annual Performance Report and public safety-data system descriptions
geography: United States; federal consumer-product safety, import, e-commerce, recall, and hospital emergency-room surveillance system

observations.period: Fiscal 2024; negotiated and implemented voluntary recalls

denominator.unit: voluntary recalls negotiated and implemented by CPSC

observations.method: CPSC annual performance report administrative performance measure for voluntary recalls negotiated and implemented; recall counts and unit counts are not injury rates.
observations.uncertainty: Recall totals depend on hazard detection, reporting, enforcement, product volume, negotiated scope, and agency/company definitions; unit count does not identify exposure, use, injury, or remedy completion.
observations.subgroup: Consumer products and firms subject to CPSC jurisdiction; product categories and affected consumers vary across recalls.
observations.counterinterpretation: More recalls can reflect more hazards, stronger detection, better reporting, larger product markets, or more aggressive intervention; fewer recalled units can reflect product mix rather than lower risk.

observations.period: Fiscal 2024; regulatory notices and e-commerce takedowns

denominator.unit: CPSC FY2024 compliance and enforcement performance frame

regulatory_violation_notices.unit: notices sent to firms for recall or other protective action

observations.method: CPSC annual performance report description of eSAFE compliance work, product sampling, platform takedown requests, and violation notices.
observations.uncertainty: A notice or takedown is an institutional action, not proof that every consumer was exposed, that a product was removed from all channels, or that a remedy reached prior purchasers.
observations.subgroup: Firms, products, importers, online marketplaces, and consumers in CPSC compliance and e-commerce surveillance activities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Takedown activity can reflect improved search and platform cooperation as well as a changing hazard surface; removal from an identified platform does not establish removal from homes or secondary markets.

import_surveillance_system.value: risk-based targeting using CPSC and Customs and Border Protection information

observations.method: CPSC performance report description of import examinations and risk-assessment collaboration with CBP, including low-value de minimis shipments.
observations.uncertainty: Examinations and targeting do not measure the total unsafe-product flow, the fraction intercepted, country-specific risk, or downstream consumer exposure.
observations.subgroup: Imported consumer products, firms/importers, de minimis shipments, ports, and consumers in US markets.
observations.counterinterpretation: More examinations may reflect capacity and targeting changes rather than a rise in unsafe imports; an examined product is not necessarily violative and an unexamined product is not necessarily safe.

observations.period: Current CPSC data architecture; 2024–2025 treatment-year availability

neiss_design.value: national probability sample of US and territorial hospital emergency departments

observations.method: CPSC public data and NEISS documentation; injury estimates require product coding, sampling weights, and query-specific definitions.
observations.uncertainty: NEISS concerns injuries treated in sampled emergency departments and is not all injury, all product exposure, recall, or consumer-harm data. Recall databases and injury estimates have different units and clocks.
observations.subgroup: People with product-related injuries treated in sampled emergency departments and products/firms represented in recall records.
observations.counterinterpretation: A recall may prevent future injury without appearing as a contemporaneous injury trend; an injury estimate may persist after a recall or reflect products never subject to recall.

related_sources.claim: CPSC public recall pages and remedy fields provide a current recall/remedy data surface with weekly updates and changing remedy availability.
CDC WISQARS supplies a broader injury context; it is not interchangeable with CPSC NEISS product-injury estimates.
CBP e-commerce/import context supplies a separate trade and border layer for interpreting CPSC import surveillance.

boundary: CPSC adds a consumer-safety institutional layer linking hazard detection, recalls, import screening, e-commerce takedowns, and injury surveillance. It does not establish product exposure, recall awareness, remedy receipt, injury prevention, firm liability, household cost, trust, or political response for the same consumer.
